# Fluorinated Elastic Copolymer with Enhanced Thermal and Mechanical Properties

## Objective of the Invention

The present invention addresses the ongoing need for improved fluorinated elastomeric materials in demanding industrial applications. Specifically, the invention aims to provide a fluorinated elastic copolymer capable of forming a crosslinked rubber that demonstrates excellent tensile strength while simultaneously maintaining a low compression set, even when subjected to high-temperature conditions. This combination of properties is particularly significant, as many conventional fluorinated elastomers exhibit a trade-off between mechanical strength and resistance to permanent deformation under thermal stress, limiting their utility in applications where both properties are simultaneously required, such as seals, gaskets, and other components exposed to elevated temperatures and mechanical loading.

## Scope of the Invention

In addition to the fluorinated elastic copolymer itself, the invention encompasses comprehensive methodologies for its practical realization. This includes detailed methods for producing the fluorinated elastic copolymer through controlled polymerization processes, as well as methods for subsequently converting this copolymer into a crosslinked rubber product possessing the aforementioned advantageous properties. These process-related aspects ensure that the beneficial characteristics of the copolymer can be reliably and reproducibly achieved in practical manufacturing settings.

## Compositional Structure of the Copolymer

The fluorinated elastic copolymer at the heart of this invention is structurally composed of units derived from three distinct and complementary monomer types, designated as monomer (a), monomer (b), and monomer (c). In addition to these polymeric building blocks, the copolymer further incorporates iodine atoms within its molecular structure, which play a critical role in facilitating subsequent crosslinking reactions and thereby contribute to the favorable mechanical and thermal performance of the resulting rubber.

### Monomer (a): Fluorinated Base Components

Monomer (a) is selected from a group of well-established fluorinated compounds known for imparting chemical resistance and thermal stability to fluoroelastomers. Specifically, monomer (a) comprises at least one compound chosen from the following: tetrafluoroethylene, hexafluoropropylene, vinylidene fluoride, chlorotrifluoroethylene, and perfluoro(alkyl vinyl ether). These monomers may be used individually or in combination, allowing for tailored adjustment of the copolymer's fundamental physical and chemical characteristics depending on the intended application.

### Monomer (b): Diene Component

Monomer (b) is defined according to a specific diene structural formula, denoted as formula (I), which incorporates variable substituents that can be selected to fine-tune the reactivity and crosslinking behavior of the copolymer. The inclusion of this diene-based monomer is instrumental in introducing additional functional sites within the polymer backbone, which subsequently contribute to the formation of an effective crosslinked network during the vulcanization or curing process.

### Monomer (c): Olefinic Component

Monomer (c) is selected from either ethylene or propylene, both of which serve as essential structural components that influence the flexibility, elasticity, and overall performance characteristics of the resulting copolymer. The incorporation of these relatively simple olefinic monomers alongside the more complex fluorinated and diene-based monomers allows for a balanced combination of properties within the final crosslinked rubber material.

Through the synergistic combination of these three monomer types together with strategically incorporated iodine atoms, the resulting fluorinated elastic copolymer is uniquely positioned to deliver the superior tensile strength and reduced compression set performance under high-temperature conditions that represent the central objective of this invention.

# Fluorinated Elastic Copolymer with Enhanced Thermal and Mechanical Properties

## Background and Technical Problem

Fluorinated elastomers are widely utilized in demanding industrial applications where resistance to heat, chemicals, and harsh environments is essential, including seals, gaskets, hoses, and other critical components used in automotive, aerospace, semiconductor manufacturing, and chemical processing industries. However, conventional fluorinated rubber materials often present a persistent trade-off between mechanical strength and compression set performance, particularly when subjected to prolonged exposure to elevated temperatures. Many existing fluoroelastomers exhibit either inadequate tensile strength for demanding applications or unacceptably high compression set values after thermal aging, limiting their long-term sealing performance and reliability in critical applications.

There exists a clear and unmet need in the art for a fluorinated elastic copolymer that can be crosslinked into a rubber material combining excellent tensile strength with low compression set, even after exposure to high-temperature conditions over extended periods. Such a material would represent a substantial improvement over existing fluoroelastomer technology, enabling more durable and reliable sealing solutions in extreme service environments.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses this need through the development of a novel fluorinated elastic copolymer produced by copolymerizing three distinct classes of monomers, along with the strategic incorporation of iodine atoms into the polymer backbone or chain ends to facilitate subsequent crosslinking reactions.

### Monomer Components

**Monomer (a): Fluorinated Olefins**
The first essential monomer component comprises one or more fluorinated olefins selected from a defined group of compounds. These fluorinated olefins serve as the primary building blocks that impart the characteristic chemical resistance and thermal stability associated with fluoroelastomers. The specific selection and proportion of fluorinated olefin monomers within the polymer composition significantly influences the ultimate physical and chemical properties of the resulting elastomer.

**Monomer (b): Diene-Type Compounds with Perfluoroalkylene Linkers**
The second critical monomer component consists of diene-type compounds characterized by the presence of a perfluoroalkylene linking group, as represented by general Formula I. These bifunctional monomers play a crucial role in the polymer architecture by introducing controlled unsaturation points along the polymer chain. The perfluoroalkylene spacer between the reactive diene functionalities contributes to the overall fluorine content of the polymer while providing sites for subsequent crosslinking reactions. The specific structure and chain length of the perfluoroalkylene linker can be tailored to optimize the balance between polymer flexibility, crosslink density, and thermal stability.

**Monomer (c): Ethylene or Propylene**
The third monomer component comprises either ethylene or propylene, which serves to modify the polymer's physical properties, including its glass transition temperature, elasticity, and processability. The incorporation of these simple olefin monomers into the fluorinated copolymer backbone helps achieve the desired balance between rubber-like elasticity and mechanical strength while potentially improving the economics of the overall polymer production process.

### Iodine Incorporation

A key feature of the present invention involves the deliberate incorporation of iodine atoms into the copolymer structure during the polymerization process. This can be achieved through the use of iodine-containing chain transfer agents or through other established methods known in the art of fluoroelastomer synthesis. The presence of iodine atoms, whether located at the polymer chain ends or distributed along the polymer backbone, provides essential reactive sites that enable efficient peroxide-based crosslinking reactions during the subsequent vulcanization process. This iodine cure site technology is particularly advantageous for achieving rapid and complete crosslinking, which directly contributes to the superior mechanical properties and compression set resistance observed in the final cured rubber product.

## Advantages and Technical Effects

The synergistic combination of these three monomer types, together with the strategic placement of iodine cure sites, produces a fluorinated elastic copolymer with a unique molecular architecture. When this copolymer is subsequently crosslinked through appropriate curing methods, the resulting rubber material demonstrates:

1. **Excellent Tensile Strength**: The crosslinked rubber exhibits superior mechanical strength characteristics, making it suitable for applications requiring robust physical performance under mechanical stress.

2. **Low Compression Set at High Temperatures**: Perhaps most significantly, the cured rubber maintains excellent sealing force retention even after prolonged exposure to elevated temperatures, addressing one of the most persistent challenges in fluoroelastomer technology. This property is particularly critical for maintaining reliable seal performance in high-temperature service environments over extended operational lifetimes.

3. **Balanced Property Profile**: The specific combination of monomers allows for fine-tuning of the polymer's properties to achieve an optimal balance between processability during manufacturing and performance characteristics in the final cured product.

## Scope of the Invention

The present invention encompasses not only the fluorinated elastic copolymer itself but also the crosslinked rubber derived from it, along with the complete methods for producing both the uncopolymer and its crosslinked counterpart. This comprehensive approach ensures that the full value of this technological advancement can be realized across the entire production chain, from monomer selection and polymerization conditions through to final crosslinking and curing procedures.

By providing a fluoroelastomer material that successfully overcomes the traditional trade-offs between tensile strength and high-temperature compression set performance, this invention represents a meaningful advancement in fluoroelastomer technology. The resulting materials are expected to find application in demanding sealing applications across numerous industries where reliable performance under extreme thermal and mechanical conditions is paramount, including automotive powertrain components, aerospace fuel system seals, semiconductor processing equipment, and chemical processing infrastructure where long-term reliability under harsh operating conditions is essential.

# Monomers: The Building Blocks of Polymers

A monomer is a small molecule that can chemically bond with other identical or similar molecules to form larger, more complex structures called polymers. The word "monomer" derives from the Greek "mono" (one) and "meros" (part), reflecting its role as a single repeating unit within a larger chain.

## Basic Characteristics

Monomers are typically characterized by reactive functional groups or double bonds that allow them to form covalent bonds with other monomer molecules. This bonding process, known as polymerization, can occur through various mechanisms, including addition polymerization and condensation polymerization.

## Natural Monomers

Many biologically important molecules function as monomers:

- **Amino acids** serve as the building blocks of proteins, linking together through peptide bonds
- **Glucose** and other simple sugars act as monomers for polysaccharides like starch and cellulose
- **Nucleotides** combine to form DNA and RNA, the genetic material of all living organisms
- **Fatty acids** can be considered structural units in certain lipid polymers

## Synthetic Monomers

In industrial chemistry, synthetic monomers form the basis for countless materials used in everyday life:

- **Ethylene** polymerizes to form polyethylene, one of the most common plastics
- **Styrene** creates polystyrene, used in packaging and insulation
- **Vinyl chloride** produces PVC, widely used in construction and piping
- **Propylene** yields polypropylene, found in textiles and automotive parts

## The Polymerization Process

During polymerization, monomers link together through chemical reactions that create covalent bonds. This process can result in different polymer structures:

1. **Linear polymers** – simple chains of repeating monomer units
2. **Branched polymers** – chains with side branches
3. **Cross-linked polymers** – interconnected networks of chains

The properties of the resulting polymer—including strength, flexibility, melting point, and chemical resistance—depend significantly on the type of monomer used and how the polymerization process is conducted.

## Significance

Understanding monomers is fundamental to fields ranging from biochemistry to materials science. This knowledge enables scientists to develop new materials with tailored properties, from biodegradable plastics to advanced medical polymers, while also deepening our understanding of biological processes essential to life itself.

# Patent Abstract

**Fluorinated Elastic Copolymer with Enhanced Thermal and Mechanical Properties**

A fluorinated elastic copolymer composition and method for its preparation are disclosed, exhibiting improved tensile strength and superior compression set resistance under high-temperature service conditions. The copolymer is synthesized from three distinct monomer units: (1) a fluorinated olefin monomer selected to impart chemical resistance and thermal stability, (2) a second fluorinated comonomer incorporating a cure-site functionality to facilitate cross-linking density control, and (3) a third monomer providing chain flexibility and low-temperature elastomeric behavior. The relative molar ratios of the three monomers are optimized to balance elasticity with mechanical robustness, resulting in a terpolymer backbone with enhanced resistance to thermal degradation and oxidative attack.

The resulting copolymer, upon curing with a suitable cross-linking system, forms a vulcanizate demonstrating tensile strength values exceeding conventional fluoroelastomers of comparable composition, along with markedly reduced compression set percentages when subjected to prolonged exposure at elevated temperatures (e.g., 200°C or greater). This performance improvement is attributed to a synergistic interaction between the monomer-derived segments, which promotes a more uniform cross-link network and reduces chain scission under thermal stress. The disclosed copolymer is suitable for use in seals, gaskets, O-rings, and other elastomeric articles intended for demanding automotive, aerospace, chemical processing, and industrial sealing applications where long-term thermal and mechanical durability is required. Methods of synthesizing the copolymer via emulsion or suspension polymerization techniques, as well as formulations for curable compositions incorporating the copolymer with cross-linking agents, fillers, and processing aids, are also described.

# Summary of Invention

The present invention relates to a novel fluoroelastomer composition possessing improved processing characteristics and enhanced physical properties following cure. More particularly, the invention provides a fluoroelastomer terminated at one or both chain ends with iodine atoms, said polymer being derived from the copolymerization of one or more fluorinated monomers together with a diene-type crosslinking monomer incorporated into the polymer backbone.

In one aspect, the invention provides a fluoroelastomer comprising interpolymerized units of at least one fluorinated monomer selected from the group consisting of vinylidene fluoride, hexafluoropropylene, tetrafluoroethylene, perfluoromethyl vinyl ether, and combinations thereof, together with a minor amount, effective to provide sites for subsequent crosslinking, of a diene-type cure-site monomer. The resulting polymer chains bear terminal iodine functionality, introduced through the use of an iodine-containing chain transfer agent during the polymerization process, such that the iodine atoms are located predominantly at the polymer chain termini rather than being randomly distributed along the backbone.

The combination of terminal iodine reactivity with pendant unsaturation derived from the diene cure-site monomer affords a fluoroelastomer that is highly amenable to peroxide curing, radiation curing, or other iodine-mediated crosslinking chemistries. The terminal iodine atoms serve as efficient initiation sites for radical-mediated crosslinking reactions, while the diene-derived unsaturated sites distributed along the polymer chain provide additional crosslink density and improve the uniformity and rate of cure. This dual functionality yields cured fluoroelastomer articles exhibiting a favorable balance of properties, including improved compression set resistance, enhanced tensile strength and elongation, reduced scorch tendency during processing, and improved resistance to heat and chemical aging, relative to fluoroelastomers cured using conventional bisphenol or randomly iodinated cure systems.

In another aspect, the invention provides a process for preparing the subject fluoroelastomer, comprising polymerizing the fluorinated monomer or monomers and the diene-type cure-site monomer in an aqueous emulsion in the presence of an iodine-containing chain transfer agent and a suitable initiator system, under conditions effective to produce a polymer having a controlled molecular weight and a predetermined terminal iodine content. The process permits control over the number-average molecular weight, iodine content, and diene incorporation level, thereby allowing the physical and cure properties of the resulting elastomer to be tailored for specific end-use applications.

The invention further provides cured elastomeric articles, such as seals, gaskets, O-rings, hoses, and other shaped products, prepared from the subject fluoroelastomer by curing with a peroxide curing agent, a coagent, and, optionally, other conventional additives. Such cured articles exhibit properties particularly suited for use in demanding environments, including automotive, aerospace, chemical processing, and oil and gas applications, where resistance to elevated temperatures, aggressive chemicals, and mechanical deformation is required.

These and other aspects of the invention, together with the advantages obtainable thereby, will become apparent from the following detailed description and the accompanying claims.

# Abstract

A fluorinated elastomeric copolymer composition suitable for low compression set applications is described, comprising a terpolymer system based on tetrafluoroethylene (TFE)-type monomers, ethylene and/or propylene units, and a specialized diene-functional crosslinking agent incorporating a perfluoroalkylene linker segment.

The copolymer backbone is constructed from tetrafluoroethylene or related fluorinated vinyl monomers copolymerized with ethylene and propylene to establish the primary elastomeric matrix, imparting chemical resistance, thermal stability, and mechanical integrity characteristic of fluorocarbon rubbers. Incorporated into this matrix is a bifunctional diene crosslinking monomer of the general structure CH₂=CH–(Rf)–CH=CH₂, wherein Rf represents a perfluoroalkylene spacer group (e.g., –(CF₂)ₙ– or related perfluoroether linkages). This diene component is copolymerized in controlled proportions to introduce pendant or in-chain unsaturation sites, enabling subsequent crosslinking via peroxide-initiated radical cure, radiation curing, or related vulcanization methods.

The perfluoroalkylene-linked diene crosslinker serves a dual function: (1) providing reactive vinyl termini for network formation, and (2) contributing additional fluorine content and chain flexibility near crosslink junctions, which mitigates stress concentration and chain rigidity typically associated with conventional hydrocarbon-based crosslinkers. This structural feature is proposed to yield a more homogeneous and elastically efficient network, thereby reducing residual stress relaxation under prolonged compressive loading.

Resulting vulcanizates exhibit a favorable balance of properties including reduced compression set values (particularly under sustained thermal aging conditions), retained elastomeric recovery, and enhanced resistance to fuel, oil, and chemical media relative to conventional fluoroelastomer or fluorocarbon-hydrocarbon hybrid systems. The tunable ratio of TFE-type monomer, olefin comonomer, and diene crosslinker content allows optimization of hardness, modulus, and low-temperature flexibility while maintaining compression set performance suitable for demanding sealing and gasket applications in automotive, aerospace, and industrial sectors.

# CROSSLINKABLE FLUOROELASTOMER AND METHOD FOR PRODUCTION THEREOF

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a crosslinkable fluoroelastomer copolymer exhibiting excellent crosslinking efficiency, chemical resistance, thermal stability, and mechanical properties, as well as to a method for producing the same. More particularly, the invention relates to a fluoroelastomer comprising a specific combination of fluoro-olefin monomers, a diene compound serving as a built-in crosslinking site, and ethylene or propylene, wherein the resulting copolymer can be crosslinked via peroxide, radiation, or other cure systems without the need for post-polymerization modification or hazardous cure-site monomers.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Fluoroelastomers are widely employed in applications requiring resistance to heat, chemicals, fuels, and oils, including seals, gaskets, hoses, and O-rings used in automotive, aerospace, and chemical processing industries. Conventional fluoroelastomers are typically crosslinked through the incorporation of halogen-containing cure-site monomers (e.g., bromo- or iodo-containing olefins) or through post-treatment processes that introduce reactive functionality onto the polymer backbone.

However, many conventional cure-site monomers present handling difficulties due to toxicity, instability, or high cost. Furthermore, achieving a sufficient crosslinking density while maintaining desirable elastomeric properties, low compression set, and processability remains a persistent challenge in the art.

There exists a need for a fluoroelastomer composition that provides inherent, efficient crosslinking capability through simple copolymerization, without reliance on expensive or hazardous halogenated cure-site monomers, while maintaining the desirable physical and chemical properties characteristic of fluoroelastomers.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention provides a crosslinkable fluoroelastomer copolymer comprising, in polymerized form:

**(a)** one or more fluoro-olefin monomers;

**(b)** a diene compound represented by the general formula:

$$\text{CR}^1\text{R}^2=\text{CR}^3-\text{R}^4-\text{CR}^5=\text{CR}^6\text{R}^7$$

wherein R¹, R², R³, R⁵, and R⁶ each independently represent a hydrogen atom, a fluorine atom, or a C1–C5 alkyl or fluoroalkyl group; R⁴ represents a divalent linking group selected from an alkylene group, a fluorine-substituted alkylene group, an oxyalkylene group, or a group containing one or more ether linkages, optionally interrupted by aromatic or alicyclic structures; and R⁷ represents a hydrogen atom, a fluorine atom, or a C1–C5 alkyl or fluoroalkyl group; and

**(c)** ethylene or propylene;

and to a method for producing such a copolymer by emulsion, suspension, or solution polymerization of the above monomer components in the presence of a radical initiator.

The diene compound (b) is incorporated into the polymer backbone predominantly through mono-olefinic addition, leaving a pendant unsaturated group along the polymer chain. This residual unsaturation serves as an intrinsic, uniformly distributed crosslinking site, enabling efficient peroxide or radiation-induced crosslinking without the need for separately introduced halogenated cure-site monomers.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

### 1. Fluoro-Olefin Monomer (a)

The fluoro-olefin component (a) may be selected from one or more of the following, alone or in combination: vinylidene fluoride (VdF), tetrafluoroethylene (TFE), hexafluoropropylene (HFP), chlorotrifluoroethylene (CTFE), perfluoro(alkyl vinyl ether) (PAVE) such as perfluoro(methyl vinyl ether) (PMVE), and vinyl fluoride. Vinylidene fluoride, tetrafluoroethylene, and hexafluoropropylene, alone or in combination, are particularly preferred owing to their well-balanced properties of elastomeric flexibility, chemical resistance, and processability.

The fluoro-olefin monomer(s) (a) are preferably present in an amount of about 40 to 90 mol%, more preferably 50 to 85 mol%, based on the total monomer units of the copolymer.

### 2. Diene Compound (b)

The diene compound (b) functions as a non-halogenated, self-contained cure-site monomer. Representative examples of R⁴ linking groups include:

- —(CH₂)ₙ— wherein n = 1 to 10;
- —(CF₂)ₙ— or partially fluorinated analogs thereof;
- —CH₂—O—CH₂—, —(CH₂CH₂O)ₙ—CH₂CH₂—, and related ether-containing linkages;
- divalent aromatic groups such as phenylene, optionally substituted with fluorine or fluoroalkyl groups; and
- divalent alicyclic groups.

Specific non-limiting examples of diene compound (b) include 1,4-pentadiene, 1,5-hexadiene, 1,7-octadiene, 1,9-decadiene, divinylbenzene, diallyl ether, and their partially or fully fluorinated derivatives, such as perfluoro(1,4-pentadiene) and analogous fluorinated diene structures.

The diene compound (b) is preferably incorporated in an amount of about 0.05 to 5 mol%, more preferably 0.1 to 2 mol%, based on the total monomer units. Within this range, sufficient crosslinking density is achieved without excessive gel formation or embrittlement, and the copolymer retains good elastomeric properties, elongation, and low compression set after curing.

Due to the asymmetric reactivity of the two olefinic ends of the diene compound (b) — one end reacting preferentially during the polymerization step and the other remaining substantially unreacted as a pendant vinylic group — the resultant fluoroelastomer possesses regularly distributed unsaturation sites along the backbone, available for subsequent crosslinking reactions, while minimizing premature gelation during polymerization.

### 3. Ethylene or Propylene Component (c)

The incorporation of ethylene or propylene (c) into the copolymer improves low-temperature flexibility, reduces raw material cost, and modifies the crystallinity and glass transition temperature of the resulting elastomer. Component (c) is preferably present in an amount of about 5 to 40 mol%, more preferably 10 to 30 mol%, based on the total monomer units.

The combination of components (a), (b), and (c) provides a copolymer having an advantageous balance of elastomeric behavior, chemical and thermal resistance, and efficient crosslinkability.

### 4. Method for Production

The fluoroelastomer of the present invention may be produced by a polymerization method comprising:

1. Charging a polymerization reactor with water and, optionally, a suitable surfactant, buffering agent, and chain-transfer agent to establish an emulsion or suspension polymerization system;
2. Introducing the fluoro-olefin monomer(s) (a), diene compound (b), and ethylene or propylene (c) into the reactor in the desired molar ratio, either as an initial charge or by continuous/incremental feeding during the course of polymerization to maintain a substantially constant monomer composition;
3. Adding a radical polymerization initiator, such as an organic or inorganic peroxide, redox initiator system, or persulfate initiator, to initiate polymerization;
4. Conducting the polymerization at a temperature of about 0°C to 100°C, preferably 10°C to 80°C, and a pressure of about 0.5 to 10 MPa, for a time sufficient to achieve the desired conversion and molecular weight;
5. Optionally employing a molecular weight regulator (chain-transfer agent) to control the polymer's molecular weight and processability; and
6. Recovering the resultant fluoroelastomer copolymer by coagulation, filtration, washing, and drying.

The molar ratio of monomers (a), (b), and (c) fed to the reactor may be adjusted according to the desired physical and chemical properties of the final elastomer, and may be maintained constant throughout the polymerization or varied to produce a gradient or block-like distribution of comonomer units.

### 5. Crosslinking of the Fluoroelastomer

The fluoroelastomer thus obtained may be crosslinked by compounding with a suitable crosslinking system, including but not limited to:

- **Peroxide cure systems**, comprising an organic peroxide (e.g., dicumyl peroxide, 2,5-dimethyl-2,5-di(tert-butylperoxy)hexane) together with a co-crosslinking agent such as triallyl isocyanurate (TAIC) or triallyl cyanurate (TAC);
- **Radiation-induced crosslinking**, using electron beam or gamma-ray irradiation to generate radicals at the pendant unsaturated sites derived from diene compound (b); and
- **Sulfur-based or other radical-generating cure systems** compatible with residual olefinic unsaturation.

Because the crosslinking sites are intrinsically incorporated during polymerization via component (b), the need for post-polymerization halogenation or the use of iodine/bromine-containing cure-site monomers is substantially reduced or eliminated, simplifying the compounding process and improving the safety profile of the overall production method.

### 6. Properties and Advantages

The crosslinkable fluoroelastomer of the present invention exhibits the following advantageous characteristics:

- Excellent crosslinking efficiency and crosslink density uniformity due to the regular distribution of pendant unsaturated groups;
- Low compression set and good elastic recovery after curing;
- Enhanced resistance to fuels, oils, acids, bases, and high-temperature environments;
- Good low-temperature flexibility attributable to the incorporation of ethylene or propylene;
- Reduced reliance on halogen-containing cure-site monomers, resulting in improved environmental and handling safety; and
- Compatibility with conventional peroxide and radiation curing systems without requiring specialized cure packages.

## EXAMPLES

*(Illustrative examples of specific formulations, polymerization conditions, and resultant physical properties, such as tensile strength, elongation at break, compression set, and crosslink density, may be provided herein to demonstrate the practice of the invention, without limiting its scope.)*

# INVENTION SUMMARY

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a fluorinated elastomer having excellent heat resistance, compression set resistance, and processability, and more particularly to a fluorine-containing elastomer copolymer having a specific monomer composition and a controlled iodine end-group content, useful as a base polymer for heat-resistant rubber articles including sealing materials, gaskets, and hoses used in severe thermal environments such as automotive and semiconductor manufacturing applications.

## Background of the Invention

Fluorinated elastomers are widely employed in applications requiring resistance to heat, chemicals, and oil, owing to the strong carbon-fluorine bond present in the polymer backbone. However, conventional fluoroelastomers crosslinked by peroxide curing systems have suffered from insufficient crosslinking efficiency, resulting in inferior compression set properties at elevated temperatures, and inadequate mechanical strength retention after prolonged heat aging. Furthermore, when the iodine content introduced as a cure-site monomer or chain transfer agent is either excessively low or excessively high, problems arise such as reduced crosslinking density, poor scorch stability during processing, or deterioration of physical properties of the vulcanizate. There remains a need for a fluoroelastomer composition that achieves an optimal balance of curability, heat resistance, and mechanical properties.

## Summary of the Invention

It is an object of the present invention to provide a fluorinated elastomer that exhibits superior heat resistance and compression set resistance while maintaining good processability and mechanical strength, by appropriately defining the constituent monomer units and the iodine content in the polymer.

As a result of intensive investigations, the present inventors have found that a fluorinated elastomer comprising specific proportions of the below-described monomer units, having an iodine content within a specific range, achieves the intended object. The present invention has been completed based on this finding.

That is, the present invention provides the following:

**[1]** A fluorinated elastomer comprising:
- (a) 40 to 80 mol% of vinylidene fluoride units,
- (b) 10 to 40 mol% of hexafluoropropylene units, and
- (c) 0 to 25 mol% of tetrafluoroethylene units,

based on the total monomer units constituting the elastomer, wherein the fluorinated elastomer contains an iodine atom in an amount of 0.01 to 5.0% by mass, based on the total mass of the fluorinated elastomer, said iodine atom being present at a terminal position and/or within the main chain of the polymer.

**[2]** The fluorinated elastomer according to [1], further comprising 0.1 to 5 mol% of a cure-site monomer unit selected from the group consisting of iodine-containing fluoroolefins, bromine-containing fluoroolefins, and fluorovinyl ethers having a cyano group, a carboxyl group, or an alkoxycarbonyl group.

**[3]** The fluorinated elastomer according to [1] or [2], wherein the iodine content is 0.05 to 2.0% by mass.

**[4]** The fluorinated elastomer according to any one of [1] to [3], having a Mooney viscosity (ML1+10, 121°C) of 10 to 150.

**[5]** A heat-resistant rubber composition comprising the fluorinated elastomer according to any one of [1] to [4] and an organic peroxide crosslinking agent.

**[6]** A crosslinked rubber article obtained by crosslinking the rubber composition according to [5], wherein the crosslinked article has a compression set of 40% or less as measured according to JIS K6262 after heat treatment at 200°C for 70 hours.

## Effects of the Invention

According to the present invention, by controlling the proportions of vinylidene fluoride, hexafluoropropylene, and tetrafluoroethylene units together with an appropriately defined iodine content, it becomes possible to obtain a fluorinated elastomer that undergoes efficient peroxide crosslinking, exhibits low compression set even after prolonged exposure to high temperatures, and retains excellent mechanical properties and processability. The fluorinated elastomer of the present invention is therefore highly suitable as a material for heat-resistant sealing rubber components required to maintain reliability under severe thermal service conditions.
